extracted.intended_audience: psychology researchers, students, and scholars studying humor, social cognition, and information-processing theories
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Wyer & Collins's comprehension–elaboration theory to evaluate or design stimuli that elicit humor by examining reinterpretation, cognitive demand, elaboration potential, and the recipient's processing goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinterpretation (the act of comprehension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The stimulus must be reinterpreted in a way that diminishes the seriousness or importance of the initial concept: the recipient first encodes the situation under one schema, then re-encodes it under a second schema in which the initial concept becomes less consequential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'diminishment' condition is critical: reinterpretations that make the situation more important or grave are not humorous (they produce dramatic insight instead). Evaluate whether the stimulus affords an alternative schema that reduces the perceived stakes or threat. Anti-pattern: reinterpretations that increase significance or add gravity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehension difficulty (cognitive demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: The difficulty of identifying the alternative interpretation matters in a curvilinear way: too easy → low humor; sweet-spot difficulty → maximal humor; too hard → failure/puzzlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess cognitive demand on a continuum. If the alternative interpretation is obvious and predictable, humor is diminished; if it requires a brief successful effort ('sweet spot'), humor is strongest; if the audience cannot find the alternative, humor fails and results in puzzlement. Use this to tune punchline complexity for the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaboration (cognitive elaboration of implications)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the punchline is grasped, audiences elaborate by considering implications, connections, and downstream meanings; the more elaborable the punchline, the more sustained the humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer stimuli whose implications 'keep unfolding' (multiple facets or extensions) for sustained amusement. Jokes resolving to a single thin point will score lower in longevity and cumulative amusement. Consider whether the punchline invites further associations, inferences, or mental play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing objectives / information-processing goal (processing set)
rubrics_metrics.description: The influence of reinterpretation, comprehension difficulty, and elaboration depends on the recipient's current information-processing goal (e.g., comprehension-set, memory-set, communication-set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the recipient's processing set: (a) comprehension-set — focused on understanding, favorable to humor from successful reinterpretation; (b) memory-set — focused on retention, may alter humor effects; (c) communication-set — engaged in social exchange, often heightens humor via social cues. The same joke may land differently across sets; design and evaluate stimuli in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion conditions (when the theory does not predict humor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory excludes: reinterpretations that increase rather than diminish significance; stimuli where no alternative interpretation can be found; stimuli processed under a strict goal where a humor frame is unavailable (e.g., during serious analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When diagnosing failures of humor, check these exclusion conditions first. If any apply, reduced or absent humor is expected rather than a failure of tuning difficulty or elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case: Ethnic humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic humor often relies on stereotyped expectations and a target whose features are reinterpreted as diminishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the theory to analyze how stereotyped schemas are flipped to reduce perceived consequences or status; be mindful of ethical and social consequences despite theoretical fit. The explanatory mechanism is reinterpretation that diminishes the target within the recipient's schema.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case: Self-deprecating humor in social situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-deprecating humor occurs when the speaker reinterprets their own behavior in a diminishing frame for audience benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how speakers frame self-aspects under a lowering schema that reduces perceived threat or status; consider social goals (e.g., affiliation) and how the communication-set amplifies effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case: Unintended humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers may reinterpret a serious event under a diminishing frame the original actor did not intend, producing unintended humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess observer reinterpretation dynamics: humor can arise post hoc when bystanders re-encode events under a diminishing schema, independent of the actor's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic question: recipient availability to reinterpret (processing set suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the recipient available to reinterpret (right processing set)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check situational context and recipient goals—if the recipient is in a processing set that does not permit re-framing (e.g., highly task-focused analytic mode), reinterpretation and thus humor will be unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic question: does reinterpretation diminish importance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reinterpretation diminish the importance of the initial concept?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly evaluate whether the alternative schema reduces perceived stakes, threat, or seriousness. If not, the response will tend toward drama or insight rather than humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic question: is comprehension difficulty in the sweet spot?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is comprehension difficulty in the sweet spot — neither trivial nor impossible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the audience must exert brief, successful effort to reach the reinterpretation. If the reinterpretation is immediate or unattainable, humor will be weakened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic question: does the punchline support continued elaboration?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the punchline support continued elaboration of implications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the punchline invites further associations and unfolding implications; greater elaborability predicts more sustained and stronger humorous experience.
